Chapter 21, part 2




You could say that, in some ways, life is about dealing with problems.

At every moment in someone's life, they are at least tangentially thinking about a problem that needs to be solved; 'My rent payment is due but I lost my job', 'My brother has a drinking problem and it's tearing my whole family apart', 'I can't find my damn car keys'. Big or small, simple or complex, serious or banal, whatever the type they are, they tend to take center stage of a person's focus.

Of all types of problems there are out there, there is one that is undeniably the best type to have.

The self-solving ones.

"AGRHHHHHHHHHH!!!!"

"OI OI OI WHAT ARE YOU-GEH!"

A blonde man wearing one of the temple priests' apprentice uniforms suddenly appeared behind Blood Golem Inosuke, wrapped his arms around his muscular abdomen, and promptly suplexes him.

"I TOLD YOU TO STOP, YOU MORON!"

The feral boar man didn't stay down for very long, in the next moment he broke away from the hold in a move that had more in common to break dancing than martial arts and jumped to his feet.

"UOHHHHHHH! YOU WANNA FIGHT TOO BLONDIE!? FINE THEN IF YOU INSIST!!!" He cried out enraged, lunging forwards with his jagged swords.

"YOU'RE STILL NOT LISTENING!!" The blonde man raged in return, the veins on his forehead nearly popping. He met the wild boar's advance with only his raised fists.

A very physical kind of anime bickering followed, filling the stale air of the cavernous tunnel with the sound of brutal fighting and screaming insults.

Just like with Inosuke, I... 'recognized' is a strong word to put there, but I could logically conclude that the blonde man was Agatsuma Zenitsu, another member of the protagonist trio of Demon Slayer. Though giving the 'Blood Golem' sign floating above his head, I could see this was another copy.

I watched the scene play out for a couple of seconds. Considered my options. And then promptly turned around and started to walk away toward the passage I came from.

It's too early for this bullshit.

"GAARRRRHHH! STOP DODGING AND FIGHT LIKE A MAN!!-- OI OI, YOU! WHERE THE HELL ARE YOU GOING!?"

"AND NOW HE'S LEAVING!! LOOK AT WHAT YOU'VE DONE, YOU IDIOT!!!"

"WHO THE HELL ARE YOU CALLING IDIOT, IDIOT!"

Ignore and walk away, that's the name of the game. Whatever weird bullshit the cast of Demon Slayer wanted with me, I'm sure it could wait after my schedule was a bit more open. Too many irons on the fire for Ōe-san at the moment anime people! I'll pick this little side quest another time! Preferably when I'm less pissed about almost being shanked by crazy boar men.

On the rocky, cavernous path I was previously traversing, the shocked miko Hinata stood around making nervous, aimless gestures, clearly rattled by the overwhelming display of anime stupidity and not knowing what to do. At the very least this meant that whatever this was it wasn't premeditated.

But there was a new figure at her side.

Ah...

Like the others, she had a 'Blood Golem' title. Her level was 50 which was a more reasonable number than the two idiots back there. She was dressed in a humble miko outfit but carried herself with an elegance that went beyond her clothes. With her dark-colored locks tightly bound in a stylized bun and her shining pupilless eyes, she looked more like a noble lady cosplaying as a miko than a real one.

I don't know a lot about Demon Slayer, having only watched the first episode of the anime and read a bit of spoilers from the manga before being dropped here, but I've seen her popping up here and there, clearly an important secondary character.

Lady Tamayo is her name, I believe.

"I apologize for the rudeness of my associates, Ōe-sama." She said with a formal bow.

Inside, I let out a grumble. Here we go. "You can say that again, despite the delinquent look I don't enjoy having strangers attacking me out of nowhere." Ok, so not all of the grumble stayed inside.

The golem woman didn't raise her head, but I could picture the fond smile from her tone. "They were being overzealous indeed. Please forgive them, this is the first time we had a champion marked by our mistress."

Champion. Mistress. "Right, and where does Nezuko fit into this? She'd made you guys I assume."

Tamayo finally rose, her pretty smile directed at me this time. As an answer, she tilted her body to the side and politely motioned to... a passage I was pretty damn sure wasn't there a moment ago. The invitation was clear.

Damn my curiosity.

-0-0-0-​

Someone was messing with the corridors.

I only managed to notice because the initial suspicion led me to pay close attention to my gut feelings and Spiritual Senses – considering the number of times these two things saved my ass this is a valid strategy – It happened every time we turned around a corner or passed through a particularly shadowy stretch, a faint, and I mean faint, like, the first few times I was sure it was my paranoia pranking my imagination, pull on my more mythical senses; magical or not, I honestly couldn't tell. It didn't happen to me specifically, but rather, the world around me. A Pulling Tension that made the hair on the back of my head stand up straight. If I had to put it into words... It was like hearing someone pulling on the strings of some musical instrument, but you're too far away to catch any sound and could only feel the tailing echo of the expected-sound that has been projected in your mind more than anything else. That, but tickling my Spiritual Senses instead.

I concluded then that the corridors were being moved without me noticing, that because I know the kind of world I live in and how it works. It certainly wasn't from any visual clue because other than that first instance and the tickling of my sixth sense, there was nothing, just long rocky corridors lit by oil lanterns and the occasional flickering light bulb.

My escort didn't say much after introducing herself and attempting some polite small talk. I think she caught on that I was trying to feel out whatever weird shit they had going on there, so she just smiled and quietly led the way, taking me further into the dark tunnels, until the vibrations and noises of the ongoing fight between golem Zenitsu and golem Inosuke faded away completely.

The changes in the scenery began to gradually happen. As we walked, the rough stone floor crudely lit by a haphazard lighting system began to smooth out, and the illumination started to become more consistent yet paradoxically more ancient. From lightbulbs and lanterns to wooden torches, then to candles with paper covers. Wood beams appeared from the dark, reinforcing the structure of the widening corridors as we went. Soon, the floor changed from stone to polished wood, and the walls from rock to sliding panels, everything around us started to look like a darker rendition of the temple above.

If I hadn't suspected that the corridors were changing as we walked, turning the last corner would have tipped me off that fact hard. Because something that wasn't here before we looked, blazed through my Spiritual Senses.

No, 'blaze' is the wrong word, it simply filled in the space. When I'm inside an illusion barrier, my senses became all jumbled up because of the immense energies forming the barrier's structure are present all around the place, pulling my senses into every direction while also engulfing all other energy sources like the light of the sun hiding the stars. This... this is like all that energy concentrated in a single point.

I blinked away some white spots in my vision that should not have been there. The energy was so great it blurred the lines between the senses. Once I repressed my Spiritual Sense skill I got used to having around all the time, I finally got to see our destination for the first time.

A shrine, one tall enough that its top almost scraped the cave's ceiling. There was some funky stuff happening with the wood as the construction around us almost seemed to bend and converge towards it but besides that and its size, the shrine was almost humble, with no ostentatious decorations or religious icons, just a simple statue that I could easy see was carved in Nezuko's likeness. It looked too small to be the Heavenly Oni herself petrified... but then again, she could alter her size, so who knows.

The other two things of note; First was the ofuda. The shrine wasn't exactly covered with them but there was a fair amount hanging from the wooden construction and one overly detailed one over the statue's face. The walls and ceiling around the shrine, however, were, with layers upon layers of ofuda papers spreading from and maybe towards the center. I could see a pattern from it, the ones closest to the shrine were uneven and disorganized, like they'd been slapped in place with a carelessness that spoke of extreme urgency, while the ones on the 'outer' parts were neatly stacked together, almost like a stylized wallpaper. I could make head or tail of their scripts in any of them; it was beyond my level.

And the other thing of notice. The jars, a series of ceramic jars about as tall as an adult man's waist were placed alongside the walls, which was rather weird and out of place, as they gave out the impression of tributes, but if this was the case then they should have been placed right in front of the shrine and not lining the way towards it. Out of everything, those were the things that made me feel most unease. I couldn't explain the feeling, they just gave off a really creepy vibe.

Putting that aside I focused on the statue.

"So, this is where she's being kept," I stated. Not the most difficult conclusion to reach.

"Indeed," Tamayo confirmed, sounding almost sad.

"I'm assuming that you want me to free her?"

"No." The woman shook her head. "To be sealed was our mistress will at the time. With no way to verify her state and not knowing the result of its removal, it is best that it remains in place."

"Okay." I frowned. "You know I'm getting tired of only getting vague answers with sprinkles of information, it's like you people get off on that. So, I'm going to politely ask and I expect a straight and complete answer: Who the hell are you people? Why bring me here? What do you want with me?" I turned to face the golem woman. "Tell me what exactly is going on, no more delays," I demanded; my voice hard.

"Of course, Ōe-sama, I apologize for upsetting you." She gave me another short bow and placed a hand over her heart. "We are... an Order of sorts, though that was never been formalized. Our faction, if you can call it that, lacks a name or formal ranks, we simply banded together and decided to act to fulfill our mistress Kamado Nezuko's best interests while she's indisposed. This may be hard to believe Ōe-sama, but we were created by our mistress' power, every single one of us. We are not human."

"I know." I deadpanned; a bit annoyed by the flowery delivery of obvious information. The woman's eyes widened a bit- and I just realized the only real indication they give out that they are not human is the game tag floating above their heads. They don't even feel different from my Spiritual Senses, so I shouldn't be able to tell.

Ah well, what's done is done. "Nezuko used a lot of you guys when she was 'testing' me and Ranma," I explained. "Didn't she tell you?"

Her reaction wasn't what I expected. Her body rocked a bit, her fingers curled over the fabric of her kosode, and a broad, uncontrollable smile bloomed on her lips, breaking her careful composure for the first time since she appeared. "So, it is true, you talked to her I-" Suddenly she drew back, visibly restraining herself, her fist rose to her mouth, and she let out a soft polite cough. "My apologies, Ōe-sama, but you're mistaken. We do not have contact with our mistress, we have never been able to. We act based on what we believe she would want the most... it's the best we can do."

"Hm, there's a story there." I crossed my arms in an unsaid demand. Tamayo nodded.

"Fifty years ago, the country was going through a most chaotic time, as you might imagine. During this chaos there was a terrible incident that gravely injured our mistress in ways that went beyond the mere physical, this caused her to enter a berserk state no one could bring her out of. The unending destruction caused by her wrath was catastrophic, growing to a point where she threatened the integrity of the great Honshu Island itself. In the face of this event and many other external factors our mistress' allies saw no other choice but to seal her within this sacred ground, with this Jiyuu-Ji Temple later constructed to contain the overspill of her power."

I compartmentalize the information feeling... not exactly surprised. I already knew Nezuko was sealed here, this was pretty obvious from our last conversation, I only lacked that context, and at that matter, I frowned. "That still a pretty vague explanation, don't you think?"

"My apologies. Only a few of us who witnessed the whole event, and our memories from back then are... foggy to say the least. We were not meant to last for as long as we did, the capability of higher thought and emotion only came later."

It took a couple of seconds for me to realize the full weight of what she implied.

"Hold on." I choked. "'Higher Thought'? You mean you weren't sapient when you were made!?"

Tamayo simply nodded.

"Our mistress wielded us like weapons. A technique to add disposable allies to a battle, to fulfill a singular, temporary purpose. Once the fight was over, the enemy defeated, and our purpose fulfilled, she dismissed those of us still left standing. In her final rampage, an army of hundreds of thousands of us was created and unleashed against everything and everyone, yet when she was sealed, there was no one left to dismiss us." The woman looked away, her expression tight as if trying to recall a long, half-forgotten memory, or a painful one. "There was a culling, enacted by the government and some of our mistress' companions, the majority of our numbers were dealt with, but they missed a few. So, we just... Lingered, wandered war-torn the country. Driven by half-formed instinct and the remaining of our mistress will. We started to gather together at some point and grew more organized, it's difficult to say when we became as we are today, but we all came here eventually."

She turned around, directing her gaze at the shrine, Nezuko's shrine. Her word trailed off for a bit as if she forgot I was there, before continuing in a softer tone.

"At first, we just wished to be closer to her. We knew we would be killed should our true nature be discovered, so we hide among the visitors, the neighborhood residents, the temple's staff." She brought her hand over her mouth and let out a peal of short, quiet laughter. "Many of us are quite good at blending in you know, and we help the ones who aren't. We were satisfied with what we had, small as it was... however..." She paused, turning to face me again, her expression was back to the calm mask of formality, no, it was colder than before. "This generation of the Seishuuin clan, the clan tasked with protection and caretaking of our mistress' seal, had proved to be more duplicitous than the previous one and began to take actions that are antithetical to their sacred duty, actions that may even hurt our mistress in the future. So, we were forced to take action against them."

Something cold stabbed my gut at her words but I kept it from my expression. Even at this shocking revelation, something pulled my attention to the ceramic jars lining the walls.

"Indeed." Said Tamayo, noticing where I was looking. She walked to the jar closest to the shrine and knelt before it. "The legend goes that once upon a time a renowned potter had his family taken by a cruel daimyō and he was forced to make a beautiful set of porcelain to decorate his court in exchange for their freedom. When the deed was done, however, the daimyō revealed he never intended to give the potter his family back and that he had them killed on the first day, before cutting off the artist's hands so he could never grant his beautiful artwork to anybody else and leave him to die outside of his castle. The potter cursed the daimyō with his dying breath and his hatred and despair were absorbed by his work. By the morning, the daimyō and his entire family were found dead, their bodies shriveled husks, with all their blood located inside the set of cursed items that would be known as 'The Blood Devouring Urns." She swept her hands almost gently over the lit of the jar - no, the urn - before opening it.

The smell hit me like a physical force. A metallic, acidic, and slightly sweet scent so intense that it left my nose and nasal cavity tingling in its wake. A distinct noise also made itself present, a quiet, yet constant bubbling that reminded me off...

"It's boiling," I noted

Tamayo nodded over the open casket of boiling blood that almost seems to glow under the candlelight.

"It is its natural state. The boiling blood of our mistress..." She looked back at me, her cold gaze against the warm candlelight giving her an intimidating profile. "She is a Lady of Blood, and her blood is her power. Yet, despite knowing this, the Seishuuin clan defile the working of her beloved companions and interlaced this travesty into the workings of her seal, so they could siphon her power for themselves to use it for their own purpose."

Ugly feelings all the fuckin' around.

It took quite a bit for me to sort them out, but I didn't let any of them show on my unmoved expression.

"... Why tell me this?" I finally grunted out.

"Because you have asked, Ōe-sama." She said, simply. "You are our mistress' champion. Among us, you hold the highest position, you speak with her voice."

"That's not what I mean!" I run my hand across my stiff hairdo, letting my scowl appear for the first time. "I'm involved with the Seishuuin clan, or at least with Shiori- fuck, does Shiori knows about this!?" Tamayo deliberately did not answer, the look was enough. Goddamn it, Shiori! "Look, my point is Shiori never did me wrong, she always stepped out of her way to help me when I needed, always tried to work with me, and was always there when I needed her. As far as I know, we're allies. You? I don't know you. I don't know your people. Yet you're dropping that you have some grudge against Shiori's family and confessing that you are actively working against them." Something clicked right there, "The temple staff, you've infiltrated her place for work, her home--"

"We did not stop there. We are working to get people inside as many Seishuuin clan's holdings as we can." The crazy golem woman added in the middle of my rant.

"Thanks for another vital piece of information. Fuck!" I hissed out in frustration. "What I'm trying to say is what is stopping me from walking right up to Shiori and telling her all about the hidden threat to her family?"

"Nothing." She said, still infuriatingly calm.

"You won't even try to stop me!?"

"You are our mistress' champion." Again with this crap. "Moreover, if revealing this information was your intention, you would not be having this outburst, you'd have kept quiet until you left this place and then move to inform her. No matter what kind of emotional attachment you have to Seishuuin Shiori, now that you have seen our plight with your own eyes and heard our reasoning with your own ears, you will not cast judgment on either side until you have all the information surrounding the circumstances." She gave me a rather pretty smile. "Because, Ōe-sama, you are a good person."

I want to punch that smile out of her face.

I reeeally want to punch her. This fucking bitch! If Ranma was here she'd already been lodged halfway through the wall.

The thing is, I suspect she would happily take that, in fact, I think she'd be ok with whatever I decided to do to her, so it would only result in more frustration.

I turned back from her and her insufferable smile and fumed silently for a bit, before directing my tightly clenched fist that could bring down a building to the cave's wall instead.

Only for the ofuda papers present around that part to shine with an azure light and bounce by strike back in a way that almost threw off my balance. It did wonders for my mood.

It took a bit, but I eventually managed to cram everything inside my Poker Face mask and rein in my thoughts into something resembling rationality.

"All you did was admit to a threatening conspiracy. What exactly are you and your faction want to accomplish? Destroy the entire Seishuuin clan?"

Tamayo shook her head. "Nothing so drastic. Our primary objective is the infiltration of the Seishuuin family's archive inside their main household. Located there are the notes of Seishuuin Abe, the creator of the technique used to seal our mistress, it is what allowed his grandson and current family head Seishuuin Zouken to modify the seal to introduce these wretched things into it, so it is essential that we have it." Despite her tone she still moved with gentleness as she carefully put the lid back on the urn, completely sealing at signs of the brilliant boiling blood inside I noted. "We shall study the notes and find some way to safely remove the cursed set, after that, we intent to destroy both the notes and the Blood Devouring Urns."

I considered that for a moment. "... That's it? No roaring rampage of revenge?"

"The assassination of Seishuuin Zouken and his son and heir Seishuuin Akehiro is our secondary objective. They have both read the notes and have the ability to work with the inner working of the seal, we cannot abide their continuing existence."

Right, I had to ask.

I pitched the bridge of my nose, too fucking early for a headache. "Not Shiori?"

"Seishuuin Shiori was never part of the line of succession and her relationship with her clan had been strained ever since Seishuuin Ena has born, it is unlikely she had access to the family's archive and secret knowledge. So no, our objective is her father and her older brother, we do not indent to bring harm upon her."

'As long as she doesn't get in our way' was left unsaid, but considering that they were talking of her father and brother...

Fucking hell.

I took a long breath, and let it out again.

"What I still don't get is what am I doing here? I get you're laying all this on me because I asked about it, but why even bring me here in the first place? You could have simply ignored me and I wouldn't even know this was happening... Don't tell me you want my help with that."

"No." She denied. "No, it's... for a completely different reason."

Tamayo stood back and turned to fully face me, if anything she looked even more serious than before.

"Ōe-sama, you and Saotome-sama... You spoke with our mistress, didn't you?" Her voice started to falter. "I...Is she well?"

…

What?

The shift in the subject was so abrupt that it took me a moment to process.

"Excuse me?"

"Ah, I apologize for my flimsy way of putting it... It's just..." I could see that now I wasn't the one having trouble keeping composure up. "It is true that there were some voices among us that promoted for your ignorance as we cannot keep reasonable information from you, so there was a risk, but you spoke with our mistress, we have a chance to verify... Our mistress, she was in so much pain when she was sealed. If we think back, we, I, can still feel... echoes of it." Her hand went up and clenched tightly over her chest. "A great chasm inside our hearts, growing ever wider, the world growing dark and cold and desolated, the light being snuffed away bit by bit, and the pain, oh the pain." Tamayo shook her head, unlike before when it was a measured gesture meant to punctuate a conversation this was a wild shake that dislodged some hair out of her bun, as if she was pulling her thoughts from a very bad place. "It is our clearest memory of that time, or first one, and it was just a fragment of what she'd experienced. The thought of her being locked on that stage all this time... We need to know if she's alright."

What the hell? What the hell happened? She was calmly talking about murderous conspiracies a moment ago, getting me all riled up and everything, now it's like she flipped.

"You... She..." I let out a long sigh. "Nezuko's fine, not in pain or anything. She built herself a little mental space thing." I thought back at the place Ranma, I, and Nezuko had our conversation. Big, but impossible to tell if it was a mansion or a big rural house. Not ostentatious but made from high-quality materials. Very nice view. "It's cozy."

And she was lonely, so much so that even Ranma who wasn't the best with social stuff was able to catch that, deep, painfully lonely. but looking at Tamayo's face brightening in a way that was more like a happy child than a proper Japanese lady, I decided to not share that.

"That's... oh thank goodness..." Tamayo breathed out, she fought to regain her lost composure but... You know those people that carry a great weight in their lives for a very long time and then the problem gets solved and they just sag? Yeah, the golem woman looked like she would fall at the slightest breeze.

"You don't even care about what we talked about, do you?"

She opened a big, brilliant smile. "It would be lovely to know. However--"

"It wasn't your priority," I spoke. "And... and you trusted me to see whatever it is done."

"You're our mistress chosen-"

"Champion, yeah got it." I brought my inventory screen over my palm and let the scroll case containing Nezuko's letter fall into it. Tamayo's eyes widened at the sight. "She wrote a letter, no idea how she did that in her sealed state." Probably a blood construct now that I think about it. "Tasked me to deliver to the yokai Tōtōsai and then come back to the temple and activate the 'favor' she put in me." I raised my other hand palms forwards and did just that. The mark was a small Japanese family crest you usually see in contract stamps - probably the Kamado's family crest as it looks a bit like a rising sun – that's the thing that literally marks me as Nezuko's champion and supposedly opens some doors in the supernatural community, but I hadn't had the opportunity to test that yet. "She'd said she would do the rest." Part of me was expecting that we would be whisked away to Nezuko's mindscape right then and there, that would be an interesting development. But alas it didn't happen, maybe I need to be asleep like before.

Tamayo's reaction was not what I expected.

Her already wide eyes grew even more and... acquired a devasted look. Her shoulders shot back up, a trembling hand raising over her mouth.

"Oh, oh dear." She turned her haunted gaze to the floor. Taking a step back. Her other hand was over her stomach, and she was threatening to fold like she was feeling sick. "My mistress... Oh no, no, no--"

"What!?" I asked sharply. Mostly to bring her out of whatever spiral she was falling under. It appears to have worked as she snapped her gaze back to me, remembering that I was there.

"My apologies, Ōe-sama." She straightened herself, body still trembling, and looked at me with despairing eyes. She had to blink away a few tears to continue. "Your quest... Our mistress quest... is impossible to accomplish... T-Ten years ago there was an incident. Lord Tōtōsai, the great blacksmith, whom mistress once regard as family, was assassinated... So, it's... Oh, she doesn't know that, oh mistress."

…

...

Err.

This is awkward.

"Yeah that's." Fuck, who do I put this? "Incorrect?" I spoke like a question. Man, I don't know what is worse, having to deal with a crying woman or one doing everything she can not to.

She kept looking at me at the edge of her breakdown, the first emotion in her eyes was incredulity. I didn't give that time to become anything else and quickly added. "I personally met Tōtōsai a couple of weeks ago. Guy's not dead."

She blinked at me; her eyes blank. I went on, waving my hand over the area behind my head. "He had this elongated skull and eyes so sunken I couldn't see them; he looked ancient as hell and had the grumpiness to match. He also had this really big cow yokai called Mō-Mō with him, which is a great name for a cow by the way. Look I'm not making this up, I swear I really met the guy."

Tamayo collapsed.

"Ah shit."

Thankfully, she didn't topple over unconscious. She just completely lost the strength in her legs and fell to her knees. I instinctively lean in to help her but held myself back at the last moment.

"I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. It's just. I-I-It's the first expressed wish of our mistress and, and we thought couldn't, but then we could. And I don't know what came over me. T-This isn't proper." The disheveled woman just sobbed and sobbed, speaking a rapid stream of words that was steadily deteriorating into nonsense.

I really put her through a rollercoaster, hm.

I tried comforting her by crouching near her and patting her back, but eventually said fuck it all the Japanese social standards like a proper delinquent and held her anyway. She went stiff at first but then pressed her face on my shirt and continued to cry, her fingers gripping my clothes wherever she could reach.

So we just sat there on the ground in front of Nezuko's shrine and waited for her emotions to settle. Meanwhile, I had time to really think about this... really tiring conversation.

She could be lying. I told myself. She had already proved she was capable and willing to manipulate me by playing with my heartstrings. This could be a ploy of her to get some sympathy, to draw me to her faction side in this conflict they want to wage against the Seishuuin.

Yet I don't think she is. That's what my gut is telling me. She gives out the impression of a noble woman or at least a woman of high social status, I've met dozens of them, Hiroshi has met dozens of them. Due to my upbringing, I could recognize them on sight and knew how they were supposed to act.

A woman like that isn't, shouldn't be fazed this easily, not by a rude delinquent boy she'd met for the first time, it was unthinkable. No, it wasn't me or my conversation skills that rip her defenses to shred, it was the topic, her mistress. Each time the focus came to Nezuko, she was incapable of keeping her composure up.

Almost like... a lost little girl, yearning for her mother...

She would not lie to Nezuko's champion, period.

… Are all the golems like that, I wonder? The reaction from the miko golem from before seems to match, but that's beyond the point.

"You do realize..." I began, after we politely separated, though we remained sitting on the floor. "That if I don't tell Shiori about the imminent danger to her father and brother's lives, I would be deeply betraying her trust."

Tamayo wiped her last set of tears and began fixing her bun, looking steadier and in control.

"Do what you believe you must, Ōe-sama, but know that we will be gone by the time you reach her. Our plans will be modified accordingly and we shall strike at another opportunity." She turned to face me, looking almost completely put together.

"Can I ask you to stop what you doing and go back to how you were, just passively tending to the shrine?"

"That is impossible, Ōe-sama. It was our negligence and conceitedness that allowed our mistress' seal to be tampered with. We will not make this mistake ever again." She bowed her head. "We shall give your due respect and obedience as our mistress' champion, but her safety and wellbeing are paramount, even above your direct commands."

"How about a compromise between the two parties? Maybe if you explain your side..."

"That would require the Seishuuin clan to be made aware of our existence, and maybe a meeting face to face. We have mighty warriors among our ranks but are few in number and are alone in this world, while the Seishuuin clan has many powerful friends and old martial alliances, we would be negotiating from a position of extreme weakness, and even if a pact could be reached between us, I fear Seishuuin Zouken would only use this opportunity to prepare his forces for a future betrayal. That man holds none of the character and honor of his father and grandfather."

No use, huh?

I looked around, trying to find ideas, and my eyes landed on the closest thing to me; an urn.

"You implied that Nezuko's health is in danger, can you tell me how exactly? Is it the urn's ability?"

Tamayo shook her head. "The urns' effect isn't the problem- the deep insult of having our mistress' blood being harvested like bound cattle aside. It is impossible for these urns to steal all our mistress' power, just like it is impossible to empty an ocean with a sake cup. The problem is the items' miasma." At my confused look, she explained. "A true cursed object will emanate a special kind of spiritual energy, one that has been tainted by the dark deeds and emotions that went into its creation. This energy only grows more intense as the object starts targeting others, with the injuries and deaths they cause fueling them with more emotions and oftentimes trapped souls, making them able to perpetuate further atrocities, creating a vicious circle." She gazed at the urns. "Just being close to a cursed object without even needing to feel or being targeted by its effects is enough to have some miasma slip into oneself. The symptoms are slow to appear, mostly just promoting dark moods, and lowering moral inhibitions, but if left to fester, it will corrupt someone at their deepest level, twist their mind, darken their heart, mutilate their souls, and even mutate their bodies in some truly extreme cases, and that's from just being around them." She pointed a finger at the complex layering of ofuda papers around the urns, and then slowly trailed towards the ones covering the shrine's surroundings. "These are tied directly to our mistress' seal; she's being constantly bathed by it."

My mouth clicked close. Okay, that sounded... really bad. And again, I'm reminded that Shiori knew about this, so again; What the fuck Shiori!?

"... But was fine, when I spoke to her, I mean, I didn't see or felt any sigh of corruption nor did she act like something was enhancing her dark emotions," I added.

It was a flimsy thing at best, as I'm not a specialist on the matter, in fact, given that I'd just learned what miasma was, I'd say I could be talking off my ass.

Yet Tamayo gave me a dazzling smile all the same.

"There is no word in all the language that exists, has existed, and will exist that expresses how relieved I am to hear that, Ōe-sama. Thank you."

Right, I... Fuck, I'm weak to this type of earnestness, I need to move on or I'll get distracted again.

"The blood, they collect it right? Do you know what they do with it?"

"This is another delicate matter," Tamayo explained. "We know it is used as magical reagents and as fuel to power some ancient barriers and defense wards across the clan's territories, but there are a lot that we weren't able to track, and the possibilities are worrying, including but not limited to the deliberate creation of Oni, a bloodthirsty creature our mistress dedicated her life to exterminate. The thought of her own blood being used to create more of them is appalling on a deep level..." The woman grew noticeably stiffer at the possibility. "... Yet their population does appear to have increased since the introduction of the Blood Devouring Urns a year ago."

Ok. Holy fuck. That's big.

Also, it confirms that the Oni from Demon Slayer are still a thing in modern times. I'm pretty sure they managed to stop them at the end of the manga, going by what I read from internet forums. Oh, and apparently Nezuko's blood can make more of them.

"Best not to dwell too much in unconfirmed possibilities." Tamayo decided. I felt like this was something that she tells herself often. I know because I'm the same way with Taimanin stuff.

"Agree," I said, closing my eyes.

I leaned my head back and let out another sigh. Not many directions I could take from here.

It would be so much, so much easier if I knew what were Shiori's feelings towards the rest of her family, if her apparently 'strained' father and brother were a pair of unredeemable pieces of shit she wouldn't mind seeing dead. I could wipe my hands off all of this, now that I understood the blood golems' reasons, I'd be happy to step back and see where the chips would lay. But as things are, Shiori and maybe Ena are sure to be affected. I cannot, I will not betray them.

But I also can not dismiss the golems' concern.

So… a third option, my last card.

"Would you be willing to momentarily stop your plans until we could find out what Nezuko's options on the matters are?"

… Apparently, the proposition of consulting with the mistress herself wasn't even crossed Tamayo's mind, given the wide eyes and slightly slacker jaw. Understandable, as they had no way to contact her. I, however, did.

So, I pressed on. "I will deliver Nezuko's letter to Tōtōsai. Heck, if we're really lucky the letter itself will contain some magical solutions to this whole debacle, but even if it doesn't, I've been instructed to come back here and activate her favor, she'd told me that she'd do the rest; the implication was that she will do what she did on that day, she will pull me up for another chat." I crossed my arms. "How about I use the opportunity to tell her about what is happening, heard what she has to say on this matter? She at least should have a say in this since it's all about her. Plus, it would give you guys the opportunity to act under her direction again."

"That's… Our mistress can…" Tamayo began before she visibly restrained herself the best she could, trying to focus on remaining objective. "Lord Tōtōsai... he had managed to keep the fact that he's alive from the wider public for a decade now, he won't be easy to track down."

"I know the exact location he will show up two weeks from now." I brandished Nezuko's scroll case. "I will deliver the letter; you can trust me on that. Afterward, I just need a day or two to come back here and talk to her."
The woman was silent for a few, long, stretched-out moments, as she considered. Before finally. "… Two weeks from now, you say?"

"Give or take a few days."

"… To act under mistress' orders, it... it would be invaluable." Tamayo drew in and let out a long breath. "Very well, Ōe-sama. We shall make no moves against the Seishuuin clan while you fulfill our mistress' task, and afterward, we will consider whatever further development you bring."

My shoulders dropped a bit with the wave of relief I felt. But I knew enough about courteous, good-faith negotiations to know that I must give her something in return.

"And until my task is finished." My hands clenched into fists, but I already made up my mind. "I'll keep what I learn here to myself, and involve no one else in this."

A compromise to stall things. On some level I knew it was a good choice, Nezuko does deserves to know now that informing her is possible. She has the right to weigh in before anything happens. Yet, it still feels like the coward's option, and it left the miasma situation unaddressed. I could only hope those 'slow to appear' effects won't show up in the next two weeks.

… And it gives me a deadline of two weeks to deal with the Ragnarok-Cardians situation before another problem pops up. I slammed a hand over my face too much of Tamayo's surprise and let out a long, drawn-out groan.

First delinquents with monsters. Now underground conspiracies against an ancient clan. How the fuck do I keep getting myself in these situations?

"Ōe-sama?"

"I'm fine." I lied masterfully and rose to my feet, making sure to slide Nezuko's letter back into my inventory. "I have to go now; I have lots to do." Lots, lots to do.

"Very well." The woman bowed, but I was already walking away and didn't look back. "Until we meet each other again, Ōe-sama." I heard her saying in a polite tone.

I almost didn't hear the following words that echoed quietly while I was further along the corridor.

"Thank you. Thank you so, so much..."

I draw in a breath and continued to walk, this time with surer steps.

Crap, I really need to develop some defenses against beautiful, older women.

…

…

And the way to the upper Temple was a five minutes walk on a completely straight line. Motherfuckers aren't even trying to hide they are messing with the corridors anymore.

Chapter 22








The air of delinquency around the NWC HQ was particularly intense today.

By that I mean that delinquents were being used as part of the decoration.

"I see you guys have caused a diplomatic incident," I remarked.

A chorus of pained groans and pitiful whines greeted me back. I gave a low whistle and took a look around the base's front ward. For every delinquent lying face-down on the ground, there's another perched funnily on top of one of the yard's weird prompts. Some were draped over the flamingos, some were crushed under a pile of garden gnomes, three were slowly rotating around by the roof of the gazebo – which could apparently rotate for some ungodly reason - and one unfortunate soul was half-hanging out of a second-floor window, limp as a rag, his upper body dangling into the open air.

Alright then

I reached down without even looking and snatched a soft drink from the vending machine that had always been at my side and definitely didn't just materialize right now.

Snapping it open, I called out.

"Touji!"

"Yes, Aniki!" came the dutiful reply from the rotating gazebo. The boy threw a salute from his upside-down position, blood trickling down his forehead.

"You didn't see my message, did you?"

"… Message, sir?"

"The message I stuck on the front door yesterday. Big sign, large friendly letters, explained the situation surrounding our guest. Look, I can see it from here."

I lifted the tip of my baseball bat from the ground and pointed. Sure enough, the sign was still there, bright and cheerful as ever.

Not the most efficient way to deliver a message, sure, but it's not like these guys have cell phones.

"Err… sorry, Aniki!" Touji said, his voice shrinking a little. The gazebo made another slow turn before his upside-down face came back into view. "We thought the Chinese were attacking!"

"Well, I can't criticize your sense of patriotism now, can I? Where is she anyway?"

As if in answer, a loud metallic screech tore through the air. The rooftop railing above bent outward like tinfoil, and an AC unit teetered for a second before plunging toward us.

I twirled my bat into a proper grip, stepped forward, and swung.

The impact cracked the air. The AC unit shot off to the side like a cannonball, ricocheted off the ground with a deafening clang, and slammed into the outer wall, missing any of my boys.

"Nevermind, I think I got the hint." I twirled the bat once more. "Touji, get anyone who can still stand out to the yard. Drag the rest. I'll patch you guys up after I deal with this."

I crouched, feeling the muscles in my thighs and calves coil like loaded springs. Then I launched myself upward faster and farther than any normal person should manage.

I still can't help feeling a flash of exhilaration each time I casually do superhuman stuff like that - At least when things are calm enough for me to think about. Striking AC units out of the air with a baseball bat, jumping over buildings... those were great ways to take your mind off heavy, stressful subjects, like an underground race of clone people plotting the demise of your close allies.

My first stop was the guy half hanging from the second-floor window. After making sure he was alive and with all limbs attached, I pushed him back inside. Then I hopped back up and finally got to the roof and around the loud noises of the ongoing battle.

Surprisingly enough, it wasn't Ranma vs Shampoo like I was expecting.

Oh, Shampoo was fighting, her silk outfit torn in a few spots, skin glistening with sweat, face locked in that razor-sharp look of concentration. The girl was clearly in combat mode. But her opponent? None other than Haruka!

My kohai was battered, bloodied, panting like a wounded animal, and with her brand new NWC uniform noticeably ragged, but she was still standing tall and throwing punches against Ranma's strongest fiancé.

God damn!

Sure, she had backup; Hachiro and Gojiro, both NWC captains, both in a similar state of disrepair as they work to tag team the stronger amazon. But still, God Damn!

Gojiro, wielding a long wooden table like a club, bellowed out a battle cry while he swung it wildly around, forcing Shampoo back several steps, while also distracting her from the flaking Hachiro, who was coming fast from behind, ready to use that bastardized savate style of his to deliver a couple of debilitating kicks on her hips and legs. But at the last second, the Amazon spun her massive Chuí - Rin told me that's what those wrecking-ball-on-a-stick things are called - in a blur. One intercepted Hachiro's kick mid-air, while the other smashed upward into Gojiro's table, splintering it with a deafening crack.

Both delinquents were sent flying, Gojiro tumbling backward, Hachiro clutching his leg in pain, just in time for Haruka to rejoin the fray.

She darted in low, feinting a strike, then used her momentum to roll past Shampoo's thrusting Chuí, springing upward into a whirling midair kick; a move I was certain came straight out of Ranma's usual arsenal.

When the hell did she learn that? I'm pretty sure she was still in the body-conditioning phase of her training; the Tendos shouldn't have taught her anything other than exercise regimes and maybe a set of starting kata, and they sure as hell wouldn't have taught her Ranma's moves, as he's from a different branch of Anything Goes altogether.

Watching my kohai and the Amazon go at it, I couldn't help but feel a stab of guilt. I really didn't know Haruka's true abilities, did I? Oh, I knew the overview, the stuff she or others told me. I knew she was getting stronger. But I never really took the time to check on her progress, or even spar with her. There was always something else more important, some sudden crisis or random chaos. I pointed her toward the places that could help her, but I never put in the effort myself. Like I was just dumping her on other people…

Fuck, all that underground clone conspiracy is getting me moody, I'll just do better for now on.

Haruka lost the fight, naturally, which might have been for the best. I really didn't want to deal with another Kiss of Death situation. It's worth noting she didn't use any wooden sword or try to channel the skills of her past life. She used only her fists.

And that's why I didn't step in until the fight was over. She had something to prove.

"Peace," I said in marginally better Chinese. Shampoo thrust one of her Chuí in my direction, eyes full of suspicion. "I assume they attacked you first?"

"Yes." She spoke with surprisingly little hostility, maybe because fighting put her in a good mood, like Ranma. "Who are they?"

"My subordinates. They missed a message I put out about you and thought you were an intruder."

Shampoo lowered her weapon and let out a huff. "Five of them are almost acceptable. The rest are trash."

I grinned. "Ah, but they only started learning how to truly fight in the last couple of weeks."

The Amazon's eyebrows shot up, and I turned to address the rest.

"Still alive, maggots!?" I cried out, and a couple of maggot-like groans answered back. Nezumi, one of my captains, poked his head out from a concealed nook, something that looked suspiciously like a grenade clutched in his hands. "Good! Y'all missed the sign."

"I… saw it," Haruka wheezed as she pushed herself upright with jerky movements. She picked up the bamboo sword that had been strapped to her back and used it as a cane to get the rest of the way up. "But the fight had already started… so I had to back them up…"

Cute. I don't doubt she was telling the truth, but she was also obviously trying to prove herself. Maybe sitting through a meeting full of people her age who were stronger than her had rattled her. I made a mental note to put her in situations where she could pick up a few W's soon.

"Nice, so if you're wondering what that sign was all about, this here is Shampoo, an Amazon, that is; a warrior woman, from China, she's going to be our guest in the HQ for a couple of days." I glanced at Gojiro and Hachiro as they staggered to their feet, while Nezumi hurried toward me, nervously clutching his grenade-thing like his life depended on it.

I barely acknowledged it. I just plucked it out of his hands and tossed it over my shoulder with enough force that it would probably hit orbit.

An explosion cracked through the air behind me. For a moment, sunlight was replaced by a toxic, emerald blaze that washed over the whole region. A sound like the wailing of dying souls tore through the air, followed by a brief whoosh, as if everything had been sucked into a single point, before the world snapped back to normal.

I suppressed any reaction and kept speaking, completely disregarding the spectacle. "So, here's what I want you to do now—" Everyone was staring slack-jawed at the sky, so I clapped my hands hard enough to make the air crack. "Pay attention, plebs! And repeat this sentence in Chinese!"

You gotta love Nerima delinquents and their ability to roll with this kind of insanity. Within moments, Haruka and my captains were giving Shampoo a martial bow and shouting, "Thank you for your guidance, senior sister!" in Chinese. Meanwhile, the Amazon kept switching between staring incredulously at the sky and gawking at the group of defeated opponents who had suddenly gone full xianxia on her.

I nodded and cast Cura, patching up most of their injuries. Not all of them, of course, fights like these are supposed to leave a mark. Once they were steady enough, I rallied the group and headed downstairs to find the others, somehow dragging Shampoo along to help haul any prone delinquents in the building out to the front yard. When we were all there, I summoned Falion, and we got to healing.

Fun fact: you don't actually need to pet Falion for her healing to work; you just need physical contact. The naughty kitty has been tricking us this whole time just to get extra pets. The psychedelic side effects still remain, though.

While I was working, the story about Shampoo spread, and a few other delinquents did the martial bow and said the words, until someone asked me what it meant, and I said it was 'Basically, thanks Aneki'. After that, everyone started enthusiastically bowing at Shampoo and thanking her for her guidance. The Amazon looked adorably confused, and even a little touched. She even started bowing back.

After that, things finally settled down a bit. Shampoo's stomach let out a loud, anime growl - much to her embarrassment - which immediately triggered a chain reaction of growling stomachs among a few delinquents. A couple of runners were sent to grab food from the nearby restaurants. The owners were… not exactly thrilled when we moved in, at least until they noticed that my boys and I were actually pretty great customers, if a bit rambunctious. Now, we're regulars at pretty much every grub stop on the block.

Soon enough, an impromptu picnic erupted in the front yard, with Shampoo seated as an honored guest, partly because she was a badass fighter, and partly because she was a cute girl.

She… actually teared up a little as she wolfed down every plate handed to her. Wait, has she been eating properly? Like, was this the first real meal she's had since coming to Japan? I don't want to believe that, but I also know how martial artists can get when they're laser-focused on fulfilling a mission they set for themselves.

"Already listen up, I have news!" I called out when the feast slowed down.

Seeing as all the NWC members were here except for Ranma, I went about retelling the information events of yesterday.

As expected, the news sends a ripple of unease through them.

"Monsters!? In Ragnarok!"

"Like the damn Kappa!"

"Oi, Oi, Oi, that sounds really bad!"

"Suzuran got trashed!? But those guys were legendary!"

"There's more," I cut in before the panic could build. "Some of the Eight Fists split apart when the event happened. Turns out people don't take too kindly to you bringing a monster to a delinquent fight." There were nods all around. "I bet there are others who still want to jump ship but are looking for a better moment, considering the ones who bailed right away got the beatdown of their lives. Their leadership is pretty fragile now. And the monsters are all centered around someone named Frigg. If you take her down, every monster goes down with her."

I let them chew on that for a moment.

"Wait, aniki, so we're going on the attack!?" Touji blurted, and that set everyone else off instantly.

"We're going to fight!? YOSH!"

"OUOHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!!"

"Fool! I told you Ranma-nii is a man!"

"SHE'S A GIRL IN MY HEART!"

At some point, you just gotta love these motherfucker. They went from being shocked by monsters to wanting to fight them just because it fits their idea of an epic delinquent showdown. Then again, they've been pretty desensitized to punching the supernatural after all the slimes, Kappa, and the random small yokai that they had to deal with.

"Pipe down, you idiots!" I yelled, forcing the room quiet again. "We're not going in half-cocked. We need an actual plan of attack. And we'll be coordinating with some allies.

"Ouohhhhhh!" Touji suddenly shot up, then froze when he realized everyone, including me, was staring at him. "Sorry, I mean, Aniki! Does that mean we'll be part of the assembly!?

"Yo! An assembly!"

"There's one happening!?"

"Of course that would be idiot, Ragnarok's been a torn on everybody's side for too long!"

"NWC will declare itself! Finally!"

Not exactly what I meant, but that was another subject I was going to get. Still…

"I'm surprised you know," I said. Rin told me the invitations went out yesterday, and we weren't included since we've been turtling.

"OUOHHHHHHHHHHHH!!"

"Old Aniki!"

"Old Aniki!"

"Does that mean he'll meet Aniki!?"

"M-Metting of Legends!"

"AN HISTORICAL MOMENT!"

"I'M SO GLAD TO BE BORN IN THIS ERA!"

"OUOHHHHHHHHHHHH!!"

"OUOHHHHHHHHHHHH!!"

Alright. The peanut gallery is starting to get out of hand.

"SHUT UP!" I kindly told them.

When they finally piped down, I looked at Touji again and nodded. "Yeah, that's the plan. We'll fortify for the next three days, then we'll go to this meeting and see what comes out of it. But regardless of the result, we're assaulting Ragnarok."

I grinned at the rest. "Time to finally put your training into action."

Silence…

"Now is the time you can shout, you fucking idiots."

All the trembling delinquents stopped holding back and erupted into a loud, deafening roar.

I could feel Haruka's eyes piercing into me. I looked her way and gestured that I'd explain later. That seemed to satisfy her.

She was thinking about the Ryōzanpaku training offer, of course, something I'd decided to keep secret for now. The reason is simple: I still don't know how it's supposed to work. Would they really be willing to train every single member of the NWC for the upcoming fight? Or just an elite group; us, the NWC captains, plus Kenichi and his crew? Logic dictates the more you divide their attention, the worse the overall result… but those guys are grandmasters powered by pure muscle and anime bullshit. Who knows what they're capable of?

I intend to nail down the details today, since we couldn't do it yesterday with half our people injured and ready to drop. Depending on their answer, I'll decide what to do with the rest of the guys.

For now, they'll continue to have Minon as a drill instructor and keep gaining experience fighting monsters in my Illusion Barrier. I wouldn't bet on them against any Cardian yet, but against Ragnarok's mooks? They'd wipe the floor with them.

"So, has anybody seen Ranma?" I asked once the atmosphere finally relaxed into something more casual after the meeting.

Shampoo, who'd been following the conversation but probably understanding only a third of it, perked up the moment she heard Ranma's name.

"No sign of him today," Haruka told me. "But that's not exactly rare."

True. Just because we're friends doesn't mean we're attached at the hip at all times. He's got his own branch of chaos to deal with; sometimes I get involved, sometimes I only see the fallout. Same with him and my own messes. And lately he's been going somewhere to train new skills, just like I've been visiting Lucretia to learn magic.

Still… after the meeting with Ryōzanpaku yesterday, I had the impression we'd be meeting today to talk things over.

… And I had… not exactly a bad feeling, but something that told me trouble was brewing. So, I closed my eyes, put my hands into a handsign, and checked my shikigami network.

A cluster of still, colorless, often blurry images bloomed in my mind. It had been overwhelming the first few times I used it, but now I could handle it, though I really need to invest in making better shikigami. So much crap I have to do.

A collective view of the entire Nerima District formed in my head like a jigsaw puzzle made of frozen snapshots. I instantly forgot most of them, zeroing in only on where a certain pigtail martial artist could be…

Ah.

That is… a thing that is happening.

I sighed, which made both Haruka and Touji look over. "It's not trouble, exactly…" It was a bit of trouble, considering the amount of property damage that was going on. Akukin Construction Company will throw another party. "Just the kind of crap that comes with emotional baggage." I looked at the middle-aged-looking middle schooler. "Touji, you stay here and oversee today's training. I want you all putting in double the effort. Haruka, you're coming no matter what I say, right?"

My kōhai gave me one of her cool-ass smirks. "You know me, senpai."

"Ranma!" Shampoo suddenly cuts in, "Ranma, I go!"

I gave the Amazon a hard look. It threw her off a bit since I've been polite for… pretty much all the times we interacted.

"Will you try to fight him?"

The purplenette frowned, her fist tightening on her sides, but soon, her shoulders slumped. She formed a hand sign and gave me a bow.

"This Amazon will respect her honorable host. She will not fight his allies for as long as he gives her shelter. This Shan Pu promises on her honor."

An honor promise, I fought to keep my face set in a hard expression and not let my eyebrow rise. That was more than I was expecting.

I nodded, "Then, you may accompany us."

Haruka was watching us closely. Suddenly, she let out a hum.

"That was some kind of oath, right?" She asked.

I froze. "Hold on… You know Chinese!"

"Ah - I mean, no? I just heard you guys speaking yesterday, so I got curious and bought some manuals on my way home. Also, I'm pretty sure that's not normal Mandarin. Not like in the books, at least."

… She got all of that in a day.

Scratch that. A single night.

I mean, I can absorb books instantly, but I'm a dirty cheater who cheats.

"… That kick, that you used in your fight. Did Ranma teach you that?" I asked the question that had been bothering me.

My kohai blushed, blushed. "Hm, no, I just kinda, pick it up?"

Okay, what the fuck. Where the hell are these heaven-defying geniuses coming from? I'm pretty sure she couldn't do that before. At least not at that level.

Oh right, she's a girl whose death could trigger the end of the world. I really should look that up when I have the time.

For now…

"So, you're picking up Chinese in record time. Does it have anything to do with being able to communicate with the cute, buxom Chinese beauty who just fell into our lives?"

Her startled yelp and the flurry of kicks that followed - accompanied by loud protests - told me I was right on the money.

Hehehe, cute kohai is cute.
