It was obvious to anyone who had watched the anime that Hibiki Ryoga was Ranma's true rival.

Sure, Ranma had two others, Kuno and Mousse, each vying for a different fiancée, but they were essentially gag characters, present more to push the episodic plot forward or set up comedic moments than to pose any real challenge. Ryoga had some elements of that too, but no other rival received as much development as he did. He was the only one with entire arcs dedicated solely to him, showing how he trained, struggled, and grew stronger, occasionally even becoming a credible threat to Ranma, even if only momentarily.

There were even arcs where the two didn't fight at all, allowing the audience to see the bond between them, a competitive one, yes, but unmistakably real. Ryoga is often portrayed less as an obstacle for Ranma to overcome and more as a true peer.

And when a peer of Saotome Ranma goes completely mad, it is noticeable.

My kohai let out a shaky breath beside me. Even Shampoo tensed at the sight

I just let out a long sigh.

"It's too much," I murmured, looking around at the devastation. "Even for our usual standards."

I could trace exactly where it started. At the corner of an otherwise quiet residential street, the asphalt had been blown open as though someone had driven a fist straight through it. Manhole covers lay twisted aside like discarded tin lids. A row of bicycles had been bent into modern art sculptures by the sheer shockwave of the Lost Boy's punch.

A nearby mailbox had been flattened against a garden wall, its metal smeared outward in a warped fan shape, as if something had ricocheted off it with unstoppable force. The nearest house bore a crater punched clean into its outer wall, fragments of siding scattered across the lawn; a single sliding door hung off its track, still rattling from the last tremor. A roadside shrine had been reduced to splinters, its stone base split clean down the middle; the offering box lay overturned in the street, coins scattered everywhere like shrapnel from the impact.

From there, the trail carved a straight line into the shopping district. Crater-like depressions dotted the road where Ryoga had landed from impossible leaps, each impact shattering storefront windows in widening rings. A ramen stand lay on its side, wheeled stools scattered across the street as if they'd tried to flee. Several shops had lost entire display walls where one of the fighters had been blasted clean through.

And the chase only escalated from there.

A set of newspaper stands lay overturned across the sidewalk, their metal frames twisted inward as though something had gripped them in passing and squeezed without slowing down. Flyers and tabloid sheets drifted through the air like startled birds, still settling from the force of the shockwaves. A small intersection farther up looked as if it had been struck by a localized earthquake. Traffic lines were warped into jagged stripes, and an entire section of curb had been ripped clean away, lying upside-down in the middle of the road with its rebar exposed like snapped bone. An abandoned taxi rested half-submerged in a fresh trench gouged across the asphalt, its rear wheels spinning lazily as the engine sputtered in protest. The driver's seat sat empty, the door left swinging open, a testament to how quickly the driver had bolted.

A parked delivery truck had been caved in from above, its roof crushed into a deep "V." Light poles leaned drunkenly at forty-five degrees, wires sparking where Ryoga's umbrella had sliced through them in a furious backswing. Even the vending machines hadn't been spared: several lay toppled, one embedded halfway into a remaining wall like some bizarre offering to the gods of collateral damage.

Finally, and perhaps fittingly, the destruction was funneled into a vast, vacant lot bordering the residential blocks, the same type that should have been the site of their first duel.

Dust clouds roiled so thickly that the boundary between ground and sky blurred. The earth was cratered like a battlefield, still steaming from the last exchange. Each blow from within the haze detonated with the sharp, concussive crack of a missile strike; shockwaves punched outward, rattling windows as far as the neighboring district.

Explosive flashes lit the murk, Ryoga's fury and Ranma's counters colliding with enough force to make the weeds along the chain-link fence ripple like grass before a storm. Every second, another blast erupted upward, a geyser of force flinging dirt and shattered concrete high into the air.

The fight had been contained, yes… but only just.

And in the center of the lot, beyond the roaring dust and the thunderclap impacts, Hibiki Ryoga fought like someone for whom the world had ended, and the one responsible was right in front of him, his voice breaking into mad screams that carried a grief sharp enough to split stone, as if that excused turning the neighborhood into his personal therapy crater.

The only silver lining in this disaster was that the chaos left no victims: Nerima's citizens had long developed an acute instinct for the local brand of mayhem and cleared out the moment the first shockwave started booming.

As we drew closer and my Battle Eye skill sharpened the chaos into something readable, I finally got a clear look at them and at their injuries.

Ryoga… looked almost undead. His shirt had been torn away entirely, leaving only his shredded pants hanging on, clearly displaying his unnaturally pale skin, with blood gushing from several wounds. A tapestry of sickly purple and yellow bruises that told the whole story of the fight so far. These weren't the usual blows or slapstick impacts Nerima was used to. Each one was a clean, debilitating strike, precision hits meant to shut someone down fast. And yet the Lost Boy had kept going, hurling himself back into the fray like the pain had never even reached him.

I could see Ranma's logic as clearly as if he'd whispered it to me. The moment he realized Ryoga was past reason, past the point where this was just another fight, he tried to stop him. When that failed, and the destruction only spread, he started escalating, each counterstrike growing harder, sharper, more vicious… not to win, but to end this before Ryoga tore the whole district apart.

Yet he still kept going.

Ranma wasn't in as bad a shape as Ryoga, but that didn't mean he'd come out unscathed. His shirt was ragged, hanging in uneven strips that clung stubbornly to his frame. The sleeves were torn almost to the shoulder, and the fabric across his chest was smudged with dirt and soot. Bruises showed through the gaps, dark and cleanly placed where Ryoga's strikes had slipped past his guard. A thin line of dried blood ran from his temple to his jaw, matting a lock of hair against his cheek.

He held himself with a rigid, coiled tension, every movement sharp and deliberate. The usual looseness in his posture was gone. There was no cocky swagger, no easy rhythm to the way he shifted his weight. Each breath was measured, almost quiet.

His eyes were the most striking change. The usual spark, the quick flicker of emotion, was gone. In its place sat a cold, hard focus that didn't quite hide the strain behind it. This wasn't Ryoga's wild rage. Ranma's anger simmered underneath the surface, tightly controlled, fighting with something that looked uncomfortably like guilt.

My best friend had clearly reached a point where he was reluctant to escalate. Even in the middle of this chaos, he still believed Ryoga didn't deserve to be on the receiving end of the trump cards he'd been developing - techniques meant for real monsters, not people. So, he was holding back, trying to contain Ryoga, trying to stall him, hoping he would burn himself out or that the strain of his injuries would finally force him to stop.

But that was proving nearly impossible. Ryoga kept getting angrier and angrier, his movements growing faster and more brutal. I could feel the rolling cloud of dark ki pouring off him, his roaring battle aura thickening the air like a storm front. It was obvious he wasn't going to stop on his own.

Naturally, I stepped in at that point, walking toward the lot as I slowly raised my arm and murmured, "Practe bigi nar…"

Just as with my healing spell, I felt my companions' eyes snap to me the moment the incantation began. Haruka's gaze was sharp and evaluating; Shampoo's was wide, shocked, and thoughtful. Four spheres of fire shimmered into existence, orbiting my forearms in slow, deliberate arcs. They drifted upward, spiraling toward my hands as the words rolled from my lips, the structure of the spell taking shape in the air.

"Sagitta Magica, Flammae Capturae!" I shouted and hurled the spell forward.

The spell burst apart the moment it left my hand, the single mass of flame splitting into a dozen razor-bright shapes. Each sphere elongated mid-flight, sharpening into flaming arrows that cut through the air with a shrill, hissing whistle. They streaked across the battlefield in an arcing fan of light and struck Ryouga in the side before he even registered my presence.

The impact hit him like a battering ram. He choked on a startled breath as the force spun him off balance, slamming him down into the dirt hard enough to send cracks spiderwebbing through the ground.

But the flames didn't ignite him. Instead, they burst into writhing strands of fire that slithered around his limbs, snaking across his torso, looping around his wrists and ankles with serpentine precision. The burning ribbons flared once, then hardened, fixing themselves to the earth, the rubble, the broken chunks of asphalt around him. In the space of a heartbeat, the spell had locked his limbs and pinned him to the ground like a captured beast.

Ryouga screamed. A raw, furious sound that vibrated with pain and outrage. He thrashed, muscles bulging, aura crackling in jagged bursts as he struggled to wrench himself free. Under normal circumstances, he probably would've torn through the restraints by sheer will alone.

But now?

His battered, half-broken body betrayed him. Every movement drew a wince; every attempt to push up made the bindings tighten with a metallic snap. Stripped of the direct focus of his overwhelming fury, his strength finally started to falter beneath the weight of his injuries. He remained trapped, helpless, still trying to break free even as the flames held fast.

"WHAT IS THIS, RANMA!? ANOTHER TRICK!? THIS WON'T KEEP ME DOWN FOR LONG! I WILL KILL YOU!!!" Ryouga raged, froth bubbling at the corners of his mouth as he whipped his head around, trying desperately to spot his hated rival from his trapped position.

I met Ranma's eyes as I approached. He looked conflicted. On one hand, I had interrupted his fight. On the other, it was clear this had already gone far beyond a simple duel and needed to end fast. I walked past him and crouched down beside the thrashing Ryouga.

He barely acknowledged me. "RANMA! RANMAAA!! YOU BETTER NOT HAVE RUN AWAY RANMA! YOU COWARD!"

I paused for a second, considering what to say, then decided to just cut through the bullshit. "So… did Akane figure out you're P-chan, Ryoga?"

That did it. His eyes, mad and reddened, snapped toward me. "Who are you!?" he snarled. Rude, he already forgot out last meeting. "Grrr, RANMA! Spreading my shame like that! You're a dishonored cur!"

"Ranma's first instinct was to keep your secret out of a courtesy you clearly didn't deserve,"

His head started wiping around again, clearly dismissing my presence and not listening to my words. So I grabbed the lower half of his face and forced him to meet my eyes. "I was the one who convinced him to tell your secret to Akane."

That got his attention.

"And now." I continued before he could react. "The sexual predator is throwing a tantrum because his victim kicked him to the curb!"

"NO!" he roared. I jerked my hand back as he snapped at it, teeth clacking shut where my fingers had been. "Lies! You liar! It wasn't like that at all!"

"I didn't give him room to breathe. "You purposefully let her pull you into her bed as a pig, Ryoga. Maybe, maybe, you'd have an excuse if it was the first time it happened. But you kept coming back. You made yourself her 'P-chan' again and again."

"RANMA! THIS IS ALL RANMA'S FAULT! HE'S THE REASON I'M CURSE IN THE FIRST PLACE—"

My fist smashed into his mouth before he could say another word. His head snapped sideways, and a tooth skittered across the dirt.

"No." My voice came out low and hard.

"You don't get to hide behind Ranma for this," I grabbed his hair and forced him to look at me. "Whatever grudge you've got with him? Whatever curses, whatever history, whatever petty revenge fantasies you're nursing? None of that excuses what you chose to do."

He thrashed against the bindings. For a moment, something cracked through the rage: a flicker of doubt, the fear of truth he didn't want to see.

"You're not pinned to the ground right now because of Ranma," I continued. "You're pinned because you decided to crawl into a girl's bed in the middle of the night. You chose to let her hold you against her breasts. You chose to keep coming back. That wasn't the curse. That wasn't Ranma. That was you."

Ryoga shook his head so hard the cords of his neck stood out. His breath came in panicked, broken gasps. "I—It wasn't— It wasn't like that! I- I—"

I almost believed him.

Not the denial - never that - but the confusion underneath it.

Some of it probably was sexual, sure. But the rest? I could see it. The affection he never got. The loneliness he was drowning in. Akane must have been the first person to treat him with any real warmth, emotional, when he was Ryoga, and physical, when he was P-chan.

In the anime, he never had friends, never mentioned family. How long had he wandered the world, lost for days or weeks at a time? Drifting from place to place, meeting people he'd never see again, forming no bonds, no deep connections, living with nothing but the obsession of getting revenge on Ranma. It wasn't hard to imagine him clinging to the first hint of kindness that appeared in his life.

But none of that mattered. Not here. Not now.

None of it excuses what he did.

I rose to my feet, brushing the dirt from my hand. Ryoga wasn't thrashing anymore. He was frozen, eyes wide, breath caught halfway in his lungs. My words had cut through the fury, slicing straight to the part of him he didn't want to see.

"As for your tantrum," I said, voice steady and sharp. "Fuck you, Hibiki Ryoga. You expected Ranma to keep your secret while you used it to deceive and abuse someone he cares about. For what? His honor? Misplaced loyalty? Hell no. We actually respect Akane too much to let you get away with it."

I tilted my head slightly, catching the faint wail of sirens drifting through the haze of dust and debris.

The police had their own unwritten rules about Nerima. Chaos like this had existed long before Ranma and his father showed up - though their presence sure as fuck turned everything to eleven. The city had adapted. Officers were trained to respond, but only to a point; most of the time they were happy to let things sort themselves out because they were hopelessly unequipped to deal with the daily insanity of this place. But even they had limits. And Ryoga's rampage? The destruction of multiple city blocks, cratered roads, overturned cars, and shattered storefronts—it was far beyond anything they would tolerate.

I looked down at him. Ryoga's furious aura had collapsed into something empty, a husk of the storm he'd been moments ago. His fight, his rage, his obsession. It was gone. He was frozen, breathing unevenly, staring at nothing.

"… You've got a choice now, Ryoga. Face the consequences of what you've done like a man. Own it up. Take responsibility for once. Or disappear. Get lost like you always do. Slip away for some distant part of Japan or to another country." I let the words hang in the air. "However, if you choose to run… You'd better never come back. Not to Ranma, not to Akane, not to anyone. You're done here. Got it?"

I released the bindings. The fire-threads sizzled and dissolved, leaving him free yet still frozen, the weight of his actions finally pressing down on him.

"In your hands now, pigboy," I said, letting a touch of levity break the tension as I started walking away.

Ranma remained close to Ryoga, pinning him with a glare that could crush stone. He muttered a few words I didn't catch - or care to - but soon he fell in step behind me. At the edge of the vacated lot, the girls waited for us. Haruka nodded, her expression cold and steady. Shampoo, probably clueless about what was going on, still read the room well enough to look appropriately serious.

Ryoga hadn't hurt or killed anyone; otherwise, Ranma wouldn't have hesitated like that. Sure, he'd caused a lot of property damage, but nothing the Akukin Kensetsu couldn't repair in a few days – They probably used magic to speed the process, now that I think about it. There was a city budget for replacing items destroyed by chaos, so that was a problem. The people of Nerima wouldn't be seriously affected; by tomorrow, life would go on, they would be back to their usual routine, with them working around the damage as best they could. The Lost Boy, however, wouldn't be warmly welcomed back into the community anytime soon.

All in all, Ryoga would likely only get a slap on the wrist, a stern talking-to that might, if he's willing, set him straight. Maybe they'd make him sleep in a cell if he's subdued enough, though it obviously wouldn't hold him if he didn't want to. His case wasn't serious enough to summon the higher authorities yet.

What happens now is internal. Maybe he'll change. Maybe he won't. I hope he does. I like him as a character, even if I've only seen his worst side as a person. But as I said… It's on his hands now.

-0-0-0-​

After a round of healing and a change of clothes, we drifted toward one of Nerima's many 'mayhem recovery stations', which is to say, a vending-machine pit stop with a couple of battered benches and a trash can that looked like it had seen better decades.

The food options were total garbage, so we stuck to drinks while I fished out the leftovers from the picnic and handed Ranma a proper meal. Me and the girls grabbed yakisoba bread from my inventory. We were better off for it.

So damn delicious.

For a while, we didn't talk. We just sat there, shoulder to shoulder on the dented metal bench, eating and drinking in the quiet aftermath. No explosions. No screaming. No craters forming under our feet.

Just a moment to breathe after the early Clusterfuck.

"How'd you do it?" Ranma eventually asked. He'd swapped his torn outfit for a fresh one from my inventory, but his NWC jacket was still draped over his shoulders.

"Hm?" I mumbled, stuffing the last bit of yakisoba bread into my mouth.

"How talk to Ryoga? I kept tryin' but he just wouldn't listen, just kept shoutin' over me."

I almost gave out a snarky response. 'My Charisma Stats is insanely high.' Or something. But I could see by the way he was hunched over, tense and frustrated, that this was really bothering him.

"… Have you ever seen me trying to talk to Kuno? Not taunting him or making jokes at his expense. Actually try to have a real conversation with the guy?"

Ranma frowned, chewing on the thought for a second.

"No, I've never seen you do it."

"I never did," I confirmed it. "Because our dear Kuno-senpai is insane. He got a set idea of how the world works and what roles everyone around him plays in it. Anything that doesn't fit gets twisted into something that does. No matter what I do or say, I'll always be the evil black wizard using spells to get in his way, and you'll always be the 'hateful villain' trying to steal his precious Tendo Akane."

Ranma frowned, probably ready to snark about that, but I continued before he could.

"Nothing we say or do will change it. We could save a puppy in front of him, and he'd just accuse us of putting it in danger in the first place." I couldn't help but smirk at the memory of that particular incident. "Happened to me once during a morning quest rush."

Ranma snorted.

"My point is, you can't reason with people like that."

You can manipulate them by playing around with their delusions, which is usually how I deal with Kodachi. But I kept that to myself.

"Ryoga? He's not as bad as Kuno... except when it comes to you."

Ranma looked up at me, unsure whether I was joking or not.

"You're his obsession, Ranma. And he won't listen to anything you say because when you meet, he's not dealing with you, he's dealing with the Ranma he's got in his head. Maybe he can be civil sometimes, but you'd better believe he'll twist whatever you say to fit his narrative. And if he's angry? Trying to reason with him is pointless."

I balled up the napkin I'd used for the bread and flicked it toward the trash like a basketball. "Listen, man… don't carry this on your shoulders. Whether Ryoga figures himself out or crashes harder, that's on him, not you."

Ranma kicked at the gravel, staring ahead with his mind far away. "…We were friends… back in middle school. At least, I thought we were."

"Then you had even more reason to call him out," Haruka said, her voice calm but firm. I'd talked to her about Ryoga before. She'd figured out a while back that he and P-chan were the same person. I guess the earlier events were enough for her to piece everything together. "What he was doing… it was criminal. A true friend confronts someone when they go down that path. You did the right thing, Ranma-senpai."

Ranma let out a slow, bitter laugh, his gaze still fixed on the uneven gravel. "…Yeah, yeah, I know. Doesn't make it feel any better, though. Feels like I just… dropped the ball. The whole mess started 'cause I didn't notice when he was pissed off at me. Maybe if I'd… been a better friend." His voice trailed off, heavy with guilt.

Haruka's expression softened, but her voice remained steady. "Ranma-senpai… feeling guilty doesn't mean you failed. It means you care. You confronted him when it mattered, when it could have gone even worse. That's what a friend does, even if it's hard."

I leaned back slightly, letting the words settle. "Look, Ranma… nobody's perfect. Middle school, high school, even now, we all mess up, miss signals, misunderstand people. The fact that you're thinking about it, that you're willing to hold yourself accountable… that's what counts. Ryoga… he's stubborn as hell, but you gave him a chance to see his own mistakes. That's more than most would do."

In the face of our affirmations from each side, Ranma rubbed the back of his neck, his cheeks coloring faintly as he glanced away. "…Hah, c'mon, don't get all mushy on me, alright? I'm not some big sap who needs pep talks." He tried to sound rough, but the faint twitch of a smile betrayed him. "…But… thanks, I guess. And don't make me say it out loud again."

Suddenly, another voice chimed in, halting and broken in Japanese. "That… Raging Demon Physic. Very rare. You be stronger the angrier you are." Shampoo, I guess she wanted to be part of the moment.

My pigtailed friend suddenly let out a squawk and shot off the bench in a leap that carried him nearly five meters into the air. "SHAMPOO!?"

Ah… he hadn't noticed she was with us. Man, he was really distracted.

"Oh, yeah. Shampoo's staying at the base for a few days," I said casually, barely reacting to his jump. I just pulled out a corn-mayo bread from my inventory and bit into it.

Ranma glared at me, eyes wide with betrayal. "What!? She told me she'd behave!" As if on cue, Shampoo stood up and offered Ranma a perfectly executed martial bow. "See? She's fine."

Ranma threw his hands up in frustration, wildly gesturing at his Chinese nemesis. "See! See! That's what I'm talking about!? How the hell do you do this!?"

I smirked. "Bitch, my charisma is over 99."

"What the hell do you mean!? That's not even a real thing, you bastard!!!"

Haruka started laughing, and soon I joined in, while Ranma grumbled and bickered beside us. Things went further downhill when a woman in the apartment above dumped a bucket of cold water from her window, instantly triggering his curse.

Eventually, I managed to explain the situation to Shampoo. Her first suggestion? "Next time see Ryoga. We kill-kill!!" Ranma's reaction was priceless; the guy practically beamed at the thought of someone else becoming the target of the Amazon's fury for once.

I then coaxed her into telling us about other cases of 'Jusenkyo curse abuse' she'd witnessed. What followed was a surprisingly funny and engaging conversation, even if parts were hard to translate, as Shampoo grew more and more enthusiastic as she realized we genuinely wanted to hear her stories.

Like the food earlier, this must be her first real conversation with someone else in months.

I could see Ranma relaxing around her, regardless of their history. He's always like that, chill enough to make friends easily and let bygones be bygones. It bites him in the ass just as much as it helped.

Overall, it was a pretty nice conclusion for the whole Ryoga situation. He will show up again, I'm sure of it, but I really hope he grows from this. I want to meet him in a non-hostile environment someday. He's still one of my favorite characters.

But that's a story for another day.
